attacks.claimAttacked: The project/operation purge rule is coherent with the accepted journal carrier.
attacks.method: Place two live operations under one project and grant generation, then purge only one operation.
evidence: permission-truth-tables.v6 defines one journal per (project, grant generation), while individual records bind Run/operation IDs.

If an operation purge emits the candidate's terminal record and refuses further appends, the other operation loses the shared journal. If it does not, the candidate supplies no terminal rule for the purged operation. The word may admits both outcomes.

attacks.method: Take a backup at sequence 40, durably append through 50, lose the primary, and restore the valid sequence-40 backup.
evidence: The accepted DR-105 order derives the next number solely from last-durable-plus-one in the journal, so the restored bytes would nominate 41 again.

The lifecycle says restore MUST NOT drop records but assigns no monotonic tail witness and does not state that every restored generation is permanently fail-closed unless completeness is proved. A normative no-drop sentence cannot distinguish the stale, well-formed backup from a complete one.

blockers.title: The purportedly answered lifecycle is nondeterministic at purge and cannot prove monotonicity after restore.
blockers.finding: permission-truth-tables.v6 makes the ordering carrier one durable journal per (project, grant generation), with operation identity carried on records, and derives the next sequence solely from the durable journal tail. v6 instead retains records for the life of a project/operation identity and gives one combined project/operation purge rule: purge does not drop sequence and may emit a terminal tombstone/archive record and then refuse further appends. That is not one implementable rule. Terminalizing for one operation closes the project/generation-wide carrier for other operations; not terminalizing leaves no stated closure for the purged operation. The optional may leaves both conforming. Backup/restore has the same missing branch: after restoring a valid but stale snapshot, the restored journal cannot know that later durable sequence numbers existed, so last-durable-plus-one can reuse them. The generic storage-loss fail-close sentence neither assigns a completeness witness nor says restored generations can never resume without one. The lifecycle therefore lists required nouns but does not close the purge or recovery state machine, while claiming DESIGN-ANSWERED and full folding of SCC-V5-B2.
blockers.requiredRepair: Anchor the lifecycle to the accepted (project, grant generation) carrier. Specify deterministic, separate behavior for operation purge, project purge, and grant-generation closure; identify which event, if any, terminalizes the shared journal and make refusal after terminalization mandatory. For restore, either assign a monotonic completeness/high-water witness with its own class, owner, writer, backup, and recovery rules, or state that any generation restored after possible tail loss is permanently revoked/fail-closed and must continue only in a new generation without sequence reuse. If DR-113 or DR-105 must choose these branches, mark them expressly reserved and stop claiming DESIGN-ANSWERED/full folding rather than inventing purge or permission semantics here.

blockers.title: Overturn restores the prohibitions but strands records written under the exception.
blockers.finding: The formal text now correctly says overturn restores the P-002-4/P-005-2 containment bars and all three boundedness instances. But after an authorized application has written the unbounded append-only journal in SC-OPS, the lifecycle's complete response is that those records are not silently rewritten. They therefore remain grant-journal bytes in a class whose restored rules forbid their containment and require boundedness. Dropping or compacting them violates the no-drop rule; rewriting or moving them has no assigned class, owner, migration, or custody contract. The exception is consequently reversible as prose but not as state. This leaves the v5 reversibility requirement only partially folded despite notFoldedThisSuccessor being empty.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define a separately authorized, owner-concurred overturn transition for existing records before claiming restoration: freeze the affected generation, assign lawful post-overturn custody and class treatment, preserve monotonic history, and state whether the old exception remains grandfathered until reconciliation. If no lawful migration exists, disclose the supersession as only prospectively or partially reversible and retain the necessary historical exception instead of claiming all three rules are restored for those bytes. Do not silently rewrite, drop, apply, or mint authority in this candidate.
